title: [GMCP 203.017.04] Adversarial and failure behavior: Complete MCP client and host
goal: Requirement GMCP-203-017-04. Close validation, authorization, isolation, privacy, bounded-resource, cancellation, concurrency, crash, retry, rollback, and recovery behavior. Add deterministic negative, attack, race, corruption, and fault-injection fixtures derived from the vector threat model. Vector outcome: GMCP is a full host, not only a tool caller: one API and CLI can connect to any supported server, discover capabilities, call tools, read and subscribe to resources, get prompts and completions, handle MRTR callbacks, tasks, Apps, authorization, notifications, progress and cancellation. Multiple servers operate concurrently with isolated identities, policies and state, and every callback surface is exercised against real reference servers. Done means production-path tests and retained evidence prove this work package; task closure or roadmap wording alone is not evidence.
limitations: Adversarial stage (`GMCP-203-017-04`) hardens `McpHost`, `DuplexPeer`, `PersistedTaskHandleStore` (`0600` Unix mode + `open_or_quarantine` corrupt-store recovery), and `parse_app_resource_summary` (`ui://` CSP/permissions/hostname validation) against malformed frames, duplicate callback IDs, notification floods, oversized payloads, peer disconnects, cross-server task replay, and policy violations; interoperability, operations, and `.M` mastery ship across `T-CODEXGMCPROADMAP-118..120`.

Per `docs/gmcp/contract-203-017.md` and zero-UI plan A9, `.agents/gmcp/evidence/VC-203-017.jsonl` and `.agents/roadmap-verdicts/VC-203-017.json` remain strictly absent until `T-CODEXGMCPROADMAP-120` (`.M` Mastery).

reuse.why: Extended existing `McpHost`, `DuplexPeer`, `PersistedTaskHandleStore`, and `parse_app_resource_summary` in `susi-wire-client` with protocol-version enforcement, duplicate callback ID detection, bounded notification queues, Unix `0600` atomic store writes + `open_or_quarantine` recovery, and fail-closed `ui://` CSP/domain validation without new dependencies.
